name: Potassium
occurrence: Never found free; combined in silicate minerals and extracted commercially from potash deposits.
majorUses: Potassium chloride as a table-salt substitute
biologicalRelevance: The main positive ion inside your cells, essential for nerve signal transmission and heart rhythm — severe imbalance can literally stop a heartbeat.
notableCharacteristics: Reacts even more violently with water than sodium does, often igniting the hydrogen gas it releases and burning with a lilac flame.
ncertRelevance: alkali metal reactivity trend down the group
whyHere: A lone 4s electron sitting even farther from the nucleus than sodium's 3s electron is even easier to lose, which is exactly why reactivity with water increases going down Group 1 from Li to Na to K.
didYouKnow: Bananas are famously potassium-rich, but you'd need to eat roughly 6,000 of them at once to get a fatal dose — the 'banana equivalent dose' is a real (informal) radiation unit because potassium-40 is naturally radioactive.
genZNote: Sodium's louder cousin. Reacts with water like it's personal, also the reason your heart keeps beat.
